newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers edge higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers edge higher in active trade.

text.p: Dirty Tanker charter activity was fairly busy on Wednesday with prompt rates in some regions edging higher despite talk of slowing demand, broker said.
Suezmax tonnage continued to find active transatlantic trade out of West Africa with rates to the U.S. Gulf for late Oct/early Nov loadings advancing five points to W107.5.
A VLCC for voyage to Philadelphia toook a firm W70.

The UK/Cont market was also fairly busy again with a million barrels booked from Sullom Voe at W70, up five points, and Aframax tonnage actively worked around the W120-W130 level with Hound Point and Sture loadings taking the top rate.
In the Western Hemisphere, Caribs upcoast trade was slower but rates were seen holding around W132.5 with E.C. Mexico liftings talked around W125.
Routes out of Mideast Gulf/Red Sea ports saw VLCC activity thinning, but brokers said rates to the West and Far East were holding steady with good enquiry for tonnage still being seen.
VLCC rates held steady with shipments to UK/Cont talked W52.5 and U.S. Gulf W55. Voyages to Japan and Singapore talked W65 and W52.5 respectively.

Asia/Pacific activity was mainly restricted to Aframax tonnage but a million barrels was booked from Dumai to the U.S. Gulf with options to E.C. Canada and USAC at fixed rates of $1.6, $1.55 and $1.5 million respectively.
Despite recent predictions of a tail off in demand, cross Med rates for Aframax tonnage were slightly firmer at around W105.
